stories.headline: Investigators say Paia fire may have been intentionally set
stories.summary: A preliminary investigation found Tuesday's Holomua fire may have been two intentionally set fires 300 feet apart, and MPD is seeking tips.
stories.text: A preliminary investigation into the origin of Tuesday's Holumuā fire in Paia indicated that there may have been two fires, 300 feet from each other, that were intentionally set. Fire officials determined that a separate brush fire was reported in the same general area the previous night. No suspects have been identified, but if you know something or have seen something suspicious, please contact NPD at 808-244-6400.

stories.headline: Chief Justice Rectenwald retires; McKenna to be acting chief
stories.summary: Chief Justice Mark Rectenwald is leaving the Hawaii Supreme Court at the end of September and Sabrina McKenna becomes acting Chief Justice on October 1st.
stories.text: Meanwhile, Hawaiʻi Chief Justice Mark Rechtenwald has reached mandatory retirement age at 70 after 15 years and is leaving the bench at the Hawaiʻi Supreme Court at the end of September. High Court Associate Justice Sabrina McKenna, who has been on the court since 2011, will begin serving as Acting Chief Justice beginning October 1st.

stories.headline: DLNR boat tour shows lawmakers healthy and declining reefs
stories.summary: A DLNR floating workshop took lawmakers and community leaders to compare sediment-impacted Kalepolepo with healthier Keālia, where participants entered the water.
stories.text: A floating workshop hosted by the DLNR Division of Aquatic Services took a boatload of lawmakers and community leaders out on the water to show firsthand in real time the difference between coral reefs in decline and healthy coral reefs. They visited Kulepulepo in North Kīhei, which is impacted by sediment runoff, and moved on to healthier sites like Kalea, Where cleaner waters have enabled coral to thrive. At both sites, participants jumped into the ocean to see the differences for themselves. According to Ridge to Reef Coordinator Tova Callender, the tour gave our leaders the chance to see the connections between Mauka actions and Makai outcomes.

stories.headline: Nene Awareness Day: how the endangered goose is recovering
stories.summary: On Nene Awareness Day, a segment shows how a wildlife biologist and sanctuary have helped nene recover from about 30 birds in the 1950s to roughly 3,000.
stories.text: My name is Raymond McGuire. I work for the Division of Forestry and Wildlife, East Hawaiʻi, as the wildlife biologist. Here we are at the Nene Sanctuary. Here we have hundreds of Nene. It's nesting season. So our sanctuary is 98 acres. We have predator-proof fencing to keep out rats, mongooses, cats, dogs, pigs, because the nene are ground nesters, and so there's a chance that their nest will be predated by these animals. stories.headline: Lawmakers push stricter e-bike rules in schools
stories.summary: Lawmakers want stricter statewide e-bike rules in schools after traffic fatalities, and DOE says banning them in high schools is harder because 15-year-olds can legally have them.
stories.text: Hawaiʻi lawmakers are pushing for stricter statewide rules on e-bikes in schools after a surge in traffic fatalities. Governor Josh Green's recent executive order calls for uniform e-bike regulations. DOE has been urged to ban faster models from campuses and promote safer transportation options. DOE says that it's harder to enforce a ban in high schools because it's legal for 15-year-olds to have them.

stories.headline: Draft assessment open for Kanaha bluff stabilization project
stories.summary: A draft environmental assessment for stabilizing a bluff makai of three Kanaha oceanfront homes is open for comment until October 23rd, with costs estimated at $2 million to $4 million.
stories.text: There is a plan afoot to stabilize a bluff fronting the shoreline Makai of three oceanfront homes in Kanaha. A draft environmental assessment is now open for public comment with a deadline of October 23rd. The project would use shotcrete reinforcement and vegetated terraces to stabilize the bluff. Costs are estimated to be $2 million to $4 million. Comments may be sent to the email below.

stories.summary: The Aloha Makena Foundation benefit golf tournament on October 19th aims to preserve Makena's history and archaeology and support living culture, with registration now open.
stories.text: Golf in Kapalua is in turmoil because of the drought, but on the other side of the island, preservation measures are being taken for Makena golf courses. The Aloha Makena Foundation Benefit Golf Tournament is making an effort to preserve Makena's history and archaeology while supporting living culture. The event is Sunday, October 19th, the fourth community event this year hosted by the Makena Golf and Beach Club. The event starts at noon and registration is now open for individual players, teams, and sponsors. For details, go to makennainfo.com.

stories.headline: SNAP benefits to Hawaii cut for a third straight year
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture is cutting SNAP benefits to Hawaii by about $8 per person per month beginning October 1st.
stories.text: The United States is by far the richest nation on earth, but the Trump U.S. Department of The Department of Agriculture is cutting SNAP benefits to Hawaiʻi for a third straight year. What they used to call food stamps will decrease about $8 per person per month beginning October 1st. According to the Hawaiʻi Department of Human Services Director Ryan Yamane, DHS is committed to walking alongside households during this transition, whatever that means.

stories.headline: Pūlama Lānaʻi shuts rock and concrete division, cutting 15 jobs
stories.summary: Pūlama Lānaʻi is closing its rock and concrete division and cutting 15 jobs, and Councilman Gabe Johnson and the ILWU criticized the decision.
stories.text: After years of building luxury vacation homes, Civil Beat is reporting that Larry Ellison's Pūlama Lānaʻi is shutting down its rock and concrete division, cutting 15 jobs, nearly 4% of its workforce. The company says it will outsource future concrete and asphalt work while encouraging affected employees to apply for other positions. Maui County Councilmen Gabe Johnson and the ILWU criticized the decision, noting the jobs were held by longtime Linaʻi residents.

stories.headline: Cool Classrooms AC program faulted for poor planning
stories.summary: Hawaiʻi's $100 million Cool Classrooms solar AC initiative was plagued by poor planning and oversight failures, and hotter South Maui schools were left out.
stories.text: More evidence that DOE is DOA. Hawaiʻi's $100 million Cool Classroom Solar AC initiative Maui was plagued by poor planning, oversight failures, and costly consultant payouts. On Maui, $26 million went to 229 classrooms in central and west Maui, while hotter south Maui schools like Kīhei Elementary and Lokilani Intermediate were left out. The flawed rollout left many campuses still struggling with heat despite the major investment.

stories.headline: Maui leads state in drownings from 2020 to 2024
stories.summary: Maui led the state in drownings from 2020 to 2024, with a rate three times higher than Oahu's, according to the Hawaii Department of Health.
stories.text: Maui has the dubious honor of leading the state in drownings from 2020 to 2024, according to the Hawaiʻi Department of Health. The rate is three times higher than Oʻahu and is the leading cause of death for kids 1 to 15 years old. A word of advice, keep an eye on your keiki at all times and always make sure it is safe to go into the water.

stories.headline: Sprout Organics baby food recalled over elevated lead
stories.summary: Sprout Organics baby food pouches sold at Walgreen's contain elevated lead and are being recalled in 28 states, not including Hawaii.
stories.text: Sprout Organics Baby food is feeding elevated levels of lead to babies. The heavy metal was detected in 3.5-ounce pouches of sweet potato, apple, and spinach baby food found at Walgreens nationwide. Exposure to lead can cause great harm to children, affecting learning and development. The product is being recalled in 28 states and thankfully, Hawaiʻi is not on the list.

stories.headline: Three Hawaii cemeteries ranked among America's most beautiful

stories.text: A new survey ranked the most beautiful cemeteries in America, and people are dying to get in. Hawaiʻi had three ranked in the top five. Hōlu Aloha Japanese Cemetery on Hawaiʻi Island was number three. Oahu Cemetery was ranked number five, and Molokaʻi's Kaupapa The settlement cemetery in its spectacular setting was picked at number four.

stories.headline: Maui Humane Society's Pet of the Week is Violet
stories.summary: Violet, a shy dog who arrived at Maui Humane Society in April, has blossomed into a sweet, mellow girl and is looking for a patient and caring ʻohana.
stories.text: Aloha kākou. Violet is Maui Humane Society's Pet of the Week. Violet came to Maui Humane Society back in April with 20 of her doggy friends, all of them hoping for a fresh start in life. When she first arrived, she was very shy. Everything felt brand new and a little But after five months of patience, love, and care from the amazing MHS team, she has blossomed into a sweet, mellow girl. Violet loves gentle pets, tasty treats, and the company of other dogs who share her calm energy. Her favorite place to relax is in her crate. It's her safe space, where she feels cozy and secure. Violet is still a little shy, but she has so much love to give. All she needs is a patient and caring ʻohana to help her feel at home. We hope that could be with you!

stories.summary: The Kahoʻolawe Island Reserve Commission set trolling dates of October 4-5 and 25-26, with annual vessel registration, catch reports, clean hulls and a $25 permit fee required.
stories.text: The Kahoʻolawe Island Reserve Commission has announced trolling dates for the month of October. stories.headline: Maui Travels sails the Canal du Midi in France
stories.summary: Suzy Gastrein travels the Canal du Midi in the south of France, describing its 17th-century engineering and lock system.
stories.text: Maui Travels. Water is the lifeblood of our world, in our taps, in our rivers and in the rain. But have you ever stopped to think about where it comes from and where it needs to be? Today, we are not just wandering the streets, we are sailing through time on the Canal du Midi. Here, I found a living masterpiece of water management, the Canal du Midi, designed to connect the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea. It's a 360-kilometer marvel of civil A dream made reality by Pierre-Paul Ricquet in the 17th century. Ricquet built a work of art, a beautiful landscape that paved the way for the industrial revolution. Today the commercial traffic is gone, but the canal purpose remains vital. The lock system works like magic as we approach our first lock. Notice the intricate mechanism that allow boats to rise and fall with the water levels. It's fascinating to see how the technology has stood the test of time. Each lock is like a gateway, taking us to different elevations along the canal. When we enter, the gates close behind us and water fills the chamber. In just a few moments, We'll be lifted to the next level and it feels like we are gliding into another world. The Canal du Midi is more than just a waterway. We are sailing through time. Amazing for 1700s?

stories.headline: Report downed seabirds to Hawaii Wildlife Center

stories.text: If you see a downed seabird on the ground and this is the time of year when you might, contact the Hawaiʻi Wildlife Center at 888-884-5000. Young petrels and shearwaters in particular get confused by artificial lights and fly in circles until they drop from exhaustion. Then they get injured or killed by cars or predators instead of flying over the deep blue sea like they're supposed to. Again, if you spot one, please call 888-884-5000.

stories.headline: US pulls back from Pacific climate efforts as China steps in
stories.summary: At the Pacific Islands Forum, the US has abandoned climate efforts in the Pacific while China positions itself as the dependable partner for islands like Tuvalu.
stories.text: The Pacific Islands Forum takes place every year in the South Pacific, where nations meet to try and solve challenges facing entire island populations sinking into the ocean. This year, the United States has totally abandoned climate change efforts in the Pacific, where sea level rise is the single greatest threat. As a result, China has taken the high ground and is now setting itself up in the region as the new dependable partner in helping islands like Tuvalu, expected to be the first to be totally engulfed by the sea.

stories.headline: Schatz says Trump has driven up prices in Senate speech
stories.summary: Senator Brian Schatz says on the Senate floor that Trump has raised the price of everything, from vegetables and coffee to household goods, and calls it a crisis of the president's own making.
stories.text: The numbers do not lie. The job market is practically frozen. Unemployment is at its highest level in four years. Inflation is rising. Home building is stagnant. The manufacturing sector is shrinking and to top it all off, Trump is raising the price of everything. Vegetables are up 40%. Coffee, 15%. Everything from toothpaste to detergent to shoes to video game consoles costs more. And more price hikes are on the way this fall and holiday season as businesses exhaust their inventories And give up on eating billions of dollars of added cost. This is America's golden age under Donald Trump. If it wasn't clear before, it is abundantly clear now, unless you are a billionaire getting enormous tax cuts and generous corporate giveaways, this economy sucks. Costs are piling up, saving money is nearly impossible, and just getting by, let alone buying a home or raising a family, And the worst part of it is, there was actually no reason for any of this. There's no pandemic, we're not in the middle of a war, there's no ongoing emergency. This is a crisis of the president's own making. And we're all paying the price. Donald Trump has made shortages the cornerstone of his economic agenda. And it is working. We now have shortages of nearly everything. Food, electricity, healthcare, workers. And with less supply to go around, everything costs more. It does not take a genius to work that out. And in fact, people have worked it out. Trump's approval rating on inflation and the cost of living is 24 points underwater. His approval rating on the economy overall is at negative 13. More than half of Americans think the economy is getting worse, and less than a quarter of Americans think it's improving. We are on a speed run to become Venezuela, and people can see it. This is a deliberate economic program. Like, there's this sense that he just wakes up in the morning and does whatever he feels like doing, and to some extent he is improvisational. But make no mistake, he has a coherent economic theory, which is we should shrink the supply of everything. He thinks it strengthens the dollar. He thinks it helps with manufacturing. And I think he thinks that the less there is of stuff, the more people have to go and petition the king for mercy.

stories.headline: Tribute marks Father Damien's canonization anniversary
stories.summary: A clip from an Akaku tribute by Daniel Emhoff recounts Father Damien's work serving Hansen's disease patients at Kalaupapa and his canonization.
stories.text: On the night of September 10th 2009, the world's attention was turned towards the man who gave his life in the service of his faith on the small peninsula of Kalapapa, isolated by the tallest sea cliffs in the world on the island of Molokai. Blessed Father Damien is now a saint. In 1873 he learned of the need for priests to serve the 700 Hansen's disease victims, and soon was on a boat bound for Kalapapa in the county of Kalawau. Because of Father Damien's unyielding compassion, Kalawau became a place to live rather than a place to die. Father Damien offered hope. He learned to speak the Hawaiian language. With the assistance of patients, he built houses, constructed a water system, and planted trees. He also organized schools, bands, and choirs. He provided medical care for the living and buried the dead. Many are at least a little familiar with his inspiring work and his sacrifice, as he cared for the lepers in Kalapapa. But few outside of Molokai truly understand the scope of all that Saint Damien did for the people of Molokai. Father Damien built hospitals, orphanages, houses, and all kinds of buildings, and by 1888 had helped to build many of the 374 buildings on the island. The compassion Father Damien had for the lepers of Kalapapa extended out to all the people of Molokaʻi. His love was truly unconditional. Today, Saint Damien continues to bless all the people of Molokaʻi. His Canonization into sainthood is bringing visitors from all over the world. Saint Damien is the first American saint. It is important to note that when Father Damien arrived, this land was still the kingdom of Hawaiʻi. So in closing, I would like to remind everyone that Saint Damien, who the people of Molokai will always affectionately refer to as Father Damien the Blessed One.

Act 96 requires that the $100 million the Green fees are projected to generate must begin distribution by next July.

stories.headline: Kula Hospital hosts 115th anniversary Hoʻolauleʻa Sunday
stories.summary: Kula Hospital holds a free community celebration Sunday from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. with food, crafts, entertainment and shuttle service from Keokea Marketplace.
stories.text: You might consider going to the Kula Hospital this Sunday from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. because the historic sanitarium is staging a Hoʻolaulea community celebration to mark its 115th anniversary. The event is free and free parking and shuttle service from Keokea Marketplace will be available. Ono grinds, crafts, handmade goods, keiki bike helmets, and all-day live entertainment are all part of the prescription. Find more information out at mauihealth.org slash kula hospital.

stories.headline: First Friday Wailuku launches Festivals of Aloha with wall art project
stories.summary: First Friday Wailuku on September 5 launches the 2025 Festivals of Aloha and invites the public to a guided wall art project in front of the ʻĪao Theater.
stories.text: First Friday Wailuku is this Friday, September 5th, and it is not only launching the 2025 Festivals of Aloha, But the public is also invited to join a hands-on, family-friendly wall art project, guided by local artists in front of the historic Eao Theatre from 5.30 to 9 p.m. The artwork will be used for the county's Wailuku garage, and the first 50 collaborators receive a free Maui Thing Wailuku Town Bridge t-shirt. There will also be music, kākou, and all of the usual festivities.

stories.headline: Maui Humane Society faces overcrowding ahead of Molokaʻi dog transfer
stories.summary: The Maui Humane Society, already housing 65 dogs with 57 in foster care, would be 40% over capacity after bringing in 26 dogs from Molokaʻi and urges fostering and adoption.
stories.text: The Maui Humane Society is struggling with severe overcrowding as it prepares to bring in 26 dogs from Molokaʻi, which would push its shelter 40% over capacity. With 65 dogs Already housed N57 in foster care, Maui Humane Society is urging the community to foster, adopt, and support its efforts to continue serving pets from both Maui, Lānaʻi, and Molokaʻi. Now it is time to meet Kira, our Pet of the Week.

stories.headline: Pet of the Week: Kira, a once-shy dog ready for adoption
stories.summary: Kira arrived at the Maui Humane Society in April, has blossomed with care, and is ready to find a loving home.
stories.text: Aloha kākou. Kira is Maui Himean Society's Pet of the Week. Kira came to Maui Himean Society back in April with over 20 of her doggy pals. When Kira first arrived, she was so shy and scared. Everything was brand new to her. People, sounds, smells, leashes, collars, even cars. It all felt overwhelming. But with gentle love and From the amazing MHS team, Kira has blossomed so much over the past 5 months. Now she enjoys walks, playing with toys, and running around with zoomies. Kira especially loves playing with her brother, Usher, and getting butt scratches from her favorite people. Kira is still a little shy when meeting new friends, but with kindness and patience, she will keep growing braver every day. Kira is ready to find a loving ʻohana who can continue to help her see how wonderful the world truly is. All of those dogs are so cool looking.

stories.summary: Three brushfires burned Tuesday afternoon, and another early this morning in Haiku closed Hana Highway in both directions before crews got it under control by 4:30 AM.
stories.text: It's fire season, and brush fires all around us are the new normal. Three brush fires kept our fire department busy yesterday afternoon. Two reported simultaneously at about 2.20 A brush fire was also reported early this morning at about 3 a.m. in the morning of And Haʻikū off of Hana Highway and Kapakalua Road, closing Hana Highway in both directions. Multiple fire units responded and got it under control as of 4.30 a.m.

stories.headline: Hurricane Kiko is a Category 2 storm east of Hilo
stories.summary: Hurricane Kiko is a category two storm 1600 miles east of Hilo, and forecasters expect it to turn west-northwest late this week.
stories.text: It is hurricane season as well, and Hurricane Kīko is now a Category 2 storm, located 1600 miles east of Hilo and moving in a general direction toward Hawaiʻi. Forecasters in Honolulu You expect Kiko to make a turn west-northwest late this week, and we will keep an eye on it for you.

stories.summary: The host says it is wise to be prepared for a fire, flood, tsunami or hurricane, then a piece shows how to make an emergency kit.

stories.headline: Kilauea erupts for 13 hours with 500-foot lava fountains
stories.summary: Episode 32 of the Kilauea eruption ran about 13 hours yesterday with 500-foot lava fountains, starting around 6:35 a.m. and ending abruptly at 8 p.m.
stories.text: Fire, wind, and now more fire. Episode 32 of the Kilauea Volcano Show acted up for 13 hours yesterday with 500 foot fountains of lava. It started up at about 6.35 a.m. and End it abruptly at 8 p.m.

stories.headline: Council member Gabe Johnson to discuss compassionate pathway bill for unhoused
stories.summary: Council member Gabe Johnson will discuss a bill creating a compassionate pathway that requires sufficient shelter before encampments are cleared.
stories.text: If you become homeless on Maui, your options are not good. Housing costs are through the roof, shelter options are limited, and affordable housing, for most people, is a joke. The county's solution to the unhoused problem is unfortunately forcible removal of encampments, Which is no solution at all. Tomorrow, Councilmember Gabe Johnson will discuss a bill to establish a compassionate pathway to deal with these issues, requiring, among other things, that sufficient shelter accommodations exist before occupants are rousted out of their encampments.

stories.headline: Essay on why people become houseless on Maui
stories.summary: An essay with interviews of people living in cars looks at why people lose housing and what it is like to be stuck in the cycle.
stories.text: There are many reasons why people become houseless and cast out into the world. Some because of the sudden loss of a loved one, a breadwinner. Some because the house got foreclosed on or the landlord raised the rent. Some because of a medical emergency or they couldn't afford the hospital or handle the high cost of healthcare. Some people are on the street because they can't make enough money to survive. We live in a society that doesn't take care of its And some people, well, they're homeless by choice. In any case, they're sick and tired of it, and what will it take for us to be sick and tired of it too? These people aren't invisible, they're human beings, deserving of our compassion and our respect. Yeah, we're back in, you know... Back in the car. Back in the car for a little while. But me and Missy here, and... Well... I haven't seen Gary in so long. I'm so relieved. Oh my gosh, Gary. Yes. Hello. How are you? Pretty good. Pretty good hanging in there, you know, keeping, I don't know, happy, I guess. Yeah, because you're stuck in a cycle of getting exited and returning to a car, getting back on list, getting used to the cycle. Yeah, yeah. I don't know. Somehow it's, you know, finding a little place to live. I'm tired of all the lies that the government tells. Of all the people bullshitting. I turn to the police. Tired of all the lies and all the shit they said they was gonna do for us. It's not just for us, it's for the kids too, the generations after us. What are you tired of? The lies, the distrust, the disrespect, and the discomfort. What are you tired of, baby? Uh... Everything. Paycheck to paycheck and for what? So we can be broke again? Like, I feel like that's all we do is work, pay bills, and broke. How does a house's person look? Uh, like me? Uh, like you? Like your neighbor? Like your brother, your sister? I don't know, I just, I don't trust nobody anymore.

stories.headline: Two lawsuits filed against Maui Preparatory Academy over transgender student policy
stories.summary: The ACLU and a former faculty member have each sued Maui Preparatory Academy, over its transgender student policy and an alleged wrongful termination.
stories.text: Transgender students are people too, which is why two lawsuits have been filed against Maui Preparatory Academy The other suit, brought by a former faculty member, The school alleges wrongful termination and that the school has violated the Hawaiʻi Whistleblower Act.

stories.headline: Hawaii delegation complains to Postmaster General about mail delays
stories.summary: Ed Case, Jill Tokuda and others wrote the US Postmaster General about persistent delays and service disruptions in Hawaii, and the postal service apologized.
stories.text: Neither snow, nor rain, nor heat, nor gloom of night stays these couriers from their appointed rounds. That is the unofficial motto of the U.S. Post Office, except for in Hawaiʻi, Which Hawaiʻi Congressmember Ed Case says experiences persistent delays and service disruptions. Joining Case in a letter to the U.S. Postmaster General were Representatives Jill Tokuda and representatives from other U.S. territories not connected to the U.S. mainland. stories.headline: MEO wins national award for wildfire recovery work
stories.summary: Maui Economic Opportunity received the Promise of Community Action Award, accepted by CEO Debbie Cabebe in Detroit, for its 2023 wildfire response and recovery work.
stories.text: Maui Economic Opportunity, or MEO, received the prestigious Promise of Community Action award from the National Community Action Partnership for the agency's work in the aftermath and the recovery phases of the devastating and deadly 2023 wildfires. MEO CEO Debbie Cabebe accepted the National Award Thursday evening at the NCAP Gala in Detroit, Michigan. MEO was one of five agencies and individuals recognized at that gathering. Congratulations to Debbie and the entire staff of MEO.

stories.headline: County warns of fraud involving Ho'okumu Hou housing program
stories.summary: The County of Maui Office of Recovery warns that Ho'okumu Hou applications go only through the county process and gives where to check official information.
stories.text: The county of Maui Office of Recovery is warning of potential fraud from third parties regarding The only way to apply for Hoʻokumuho is directly through the county process. So please check the official program information from the County of Maui and the Hoʻokumuho program staff by visiting hoʻokumuho.mauicounty.gov online or in person at the resource centers in both Haleakalā, Kahului, or at the Resource Center in Lahaina Gateway Shopping Center.

stories.headline: Reports detail Hawaiʻi drowning statistics and Maui ocean safety gaps
stories.summary: Civil Beat and MauiNow report little state drowning-prevention funding and only 12 lifeguard towers in Maui County, where 71% of 207 fatal drownings from 2015 to 2024 were tourists.
stories.text: Civil Beat continues to report shocking drowning statistics for Hawaiʻi. Less than 0.01 percent of the state 2024 budget went to drowning prevention, and the state's Signed Placement Task Force hasn't met in over a decade. According to Maui Now, Maui County has systemic ocean safety challenges, with only 12 lifeguard towers and 87 lifeguards covering all of our world-famous beaches. From 2015 through 2024, 71% of the 207 fatal ocean drownings in Maui County were tourists.

stories.headline: State launches Engage.Hawaii.gov civic engagement website
stories.summary: A new state website for transparency and civic engagement has launched, starting with the issue of future US Army land leases in Hawaiʻi.
stories.text: Engage.Hawaii.gov. That is a new state-sponsored public website designed to promote government transparency and encourage civic engagement on some of the most pressing issues facing the state, and that has been launched. The website will make its debut by tackling the issue of future U.S. Army land leases in Hawaii, which will have widespread ramifications for

stories.headline: State jobs open to students within three months of graduating
stories.summary: Governor Green announced that applicants on track to earn a bachelor's degree in December can now apply for open state jobs pending verification.
stories.text: Governor Green has announced that as of now, applicants who are on track to obtain a bachelor's degree in December of this year may begin to apply for open state jobs. The Department of Human Resources will accept applications pending verification of a bachelor's degree For applicants who indicate that they are within three months of graduation. This will allow college students to line up a state career without delay after picking up that diploma.

stories.headline: Maui Travels visits Bears Ears National Monument in Utah
stories.summary: Lance Holter tours Bears Ears in southern Utah, covering its cliff dwellings, the ancestral Puebloans who vanished around 1200 and its meaning to Native peoples.
stories.text: On this edition of Maui Travels, Lance Holter takes us to the nation's newest national monument in southern Utah along the Arizona border. The Native Americans who lived there a long time ago called it Bear's Ears because those two buttes off in the distance made them think of a bear's head sticking up over the horizon. Cute, eh? Nine hundred years ago, this cliff dwelling was the home of the Anazazi, ancestors of The Hopi and the Zuni and now a place of worship and medicine gathering for the Navajo, the Zuni, the Hopi and the Utes. Somewhere around the year 1200 something really strange happened. 35,000 people disappeared. One of the greatest vanishing acts in human history. They just walked away. They left their cooking pots and all their belongings behind. They just got up and split like they'd be back in a couple of hours. They never returned. No one Who knows why? Current speculation is that it may have been a drastic drought and there is evidence that some may have resorted to cannibalism. When there is water, it nourishes what Lance calls the happy cottonwood trees. Its soft wood come to life in the carving of the kachina dolls. But it was mainly yucca that was used in the construction of the pukas or Keevas on the side of the cliffs. Nice view. This is probably a granary where they stored corn and squash and pumpkins and beans, but Lance Holter is a construction guy so he got carried away with square knots. One thousand year old square knots. Alright, that's more like it. If you look closely you can see the hand prints of the Nauho Dishkish, Places to be left alone. Thanks for bearing with us at Bears Ears, and we'll see you next time on Maui Travels.

stories.summary: Officer Suzanne O was laid to rest, and the murder trial of Clembert Kaneholani is scheduled for February 2, 2026, with a pre-trial conference on October 6th.
stories.text: Slain Maui police officer Suzanne Oh was laid to rest yesterday. Chief Pelletier said that Officer Suzanne Oh was the finest of us. Everyone that knew her loved her. She made the community Hawaiʻi is now a better place. As for the man who took her life, Klembert Kaneholani, his murder trial is now scheduled for February 2nd, 2026, and a pre-trial conference will be held this October 6th.

stories.summary: Ghost guns like the one used in the shooting of Officer O are virtually untraceable because the parts are easy to buy online.
stories.text: Hawaiʻi has some of the strongest gun laws in the country. Nevertheless, ghost guns, like the one used in the fatal shooting of Officer O, are almost impossible to regulate because the unassembled parts to make them are easy to buy on the internet. stories.headline: Maui Memorial ER entrance moves temporarily for new unit
stories.summary: Maui Memorial Medical Center is building a Clinical Decision Unit with 12 observation beds, temporarily moving the ER entrance starting September 3rd.
stories.text: Maui Memorial Medical Center is beginning construction on the new Clinical Decision Unit, which will temporarily relocate the Emergency Department entrance beginning tomorrow, September 3rd. The new ER entrance is located immediately to the left of the existing ER entrance. This new specialized unit will provide 12 additional observation beds to help reduce emergency room wait times. Parking and valet services for the ER will remain the same.

stories.headline: Billionaires stay while Hawaii's workers leave for cheaper states
stories.summary: After a rally at Makena, the story says Hawaii's labor force keeps shrinking as younger workers leave, and union officials say training programs need good-paying jobs.
stories.text: A billionaires off the beach rally took place this past Saturday, Labor Day weekend, out at Makena. But the billionaires are still there, because they know full well this is paradise, and they're not leaving. But Hawaiʻi's labor force is. As the population ages, retires, and then dies, younger workers continue to leave Hawaiʻi for more affordable states. Training programs can help, but according to union officials, those programs won't pay off if there are not enough good-paying jobs. Even the billionaires may have to worry if there are not enough workers to serve their every whim, or if there are not enough beaches for their mansions.

stories.headline: Federal cut hits UH sea level research as Maui beaches erode
stories.summary: A cut of $3 million in federal funds threatens University of Hawaii sea level research, followed by a package on Maui beach erosion and the need to plan now.
stories.text: Over the centuries our beaches change with the seasons and we expect that. We had a recent ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi, Kūpuna, ʻohana, mālama, kuleana, mele, oli, hula, kumu, hula, kumu, kumu, ʻāina, mālama, kuleana, mele, kumu, kumu, kumu, kumu, kumu, kumu, kumu, kumu, Check out these sandbags on the ocean side of two west side hotels, the Kānappali Beach Club and Valley Isle Resort. What will we do when we run out of beach with the sand to replenish? As the ocean advances upon us inch by inch every year, will we have the foresight to make a plan to abandon billions of dollars worth of real estate so there will be beaches on Maui in our future? Some places, like the Atolls of Tuvalu, home to an entire civilization, may be the first place to be completely swallowed by the ocean in the next 30 to 50 years. Maui, with its 10,000 foot volcano, isn't going to go anywhere, but our beaches might, unless we begin the planning process now. If we don't, in 100 or 200 years, there won't be any beaches for us or anyone else to bask on. Just a rocky fortress in the middle of the sea.

stories.headline: Mike Victorino named Grand Marshal of Maui County Fair Parade
stories.summary: Former mayor Mike Victorino will lead the Maui County Fair Parade in Kahului on October 2nd, and participant applications are open through September 12th.
stories.text: There's a new marshal in town for the long-absent Maui County Fair Parade, and you couldn't ask for a better choice. Avid Fair advocate and former mayor Mike Victorino has been chosen as the Grand Marshal to lead the Maui County Fair Parade in Kaho'olui on October 2nd. The parade always kicks off the four-day affair, and the 98th fair is no exception. Applications for participants are being accepted from now through Friday, September 12th. Google Maui County Parade Or visit themauifair.com for details.

stories.headline: International travel to the U.S. slump may last, including Hawaii
stories.summary: Travel experts say tariffs, immigration crackdown and annexation threats are keeping visitors away, and a World Travel and Tourism Council study found the U.S. losing global appeal.
stories.text: A downturn in international travel to the U.S. may last long after summer is gone. Hawaiʻi is no exception. Travel experts are warning that Trump's tariffs, immigration crackdown, and threats to annex Canada and Greenland are a major factor in keeping visitors away. A recent World Travel and Tourism Council study found that the global appeal of the United States is slipping and said that the government is, quote, putting up the closed sign.

stories.headline: Holo Holo Mom visits Kihei whale sanctuary's last summer Saturday
stories.summary: Volunteers at the Hawaiian Islands Humpback Whale National Marine Sanctuary Visitor Center hosted a final sanctuary Saturday with ocean education activities for keiki.
stories.text: On Saturday, August 30th, volunteers at the Hawaiian Islands Humpback Whale National Marine Sanctuary Visitor Center hosted their last sanctuary Saturday on the last Saturday of The last month of the summer in Kīhei. Volunteers spent their time educating our littlest residents on the beauty of our oceans. The creatures that inhabit them, how to respect and protect them, like seeing the size of some marine debris, also featuring toys and videos of our favorite sea creatures, as well as how to respect and protect the oceans as a whole. Even getting to see the beauty of turtles with crafts and puzzles next to coral displays. And the volunteers even attempted to read to us. After our fun inside, outside. The trades were rather light, but the tide was high. So without sea turtles attracting crowds, we enjoyed the fish pond beach to ourselves.

stories.headline: Rat lungworm disease remains a statewide risk in Hawaii
stories.summary: A Department of Health doctor says residents and visitors face equal risk, and a 2022 UH study found 32 species that can cause the disease in humans.
stories.text: One thing you don't want to put on the travel poster is the rat lungworm parasite that you can get from accidentally eating the slime of slugs, snails, or unwashed raw vegetables. The rat lungworm disease is alive and well in Hawaiʻi, and according to Department of Health Dr. Lauren Pang, residents and visitors are at equal risk. A 2022 UH study found that 32 species of freshwater shrimp, crayfish, crabs, flatworms, fish, sea snakes, frogs, toads, lizards, and centipedes can all cause rat lungworm disease in humans.

stories.headline: Stranded dolphins carry bacterial infection that can spread to humans
stories.summary: UH researchers found three stranded striped dolphins in East Oahu with Brucella ceti, and the public is asked to report dead or distressed marine mammals to a hotline.
stories.text: Not only that, UH researchers have discovered that you can even get flu-like symptoms from 3 stranded striped dolphins in East Oahu have a bacterial infection called bruceliceti that can spread from animals to humans. The ailment can be dangerous to humans who touch infected animals, whether distressed in the ocean or stranded on the beach. The public is asked to report sightings of dead or distressed marine mammals to the toll-free hotline. And that hotline number is 1-888-256-9840.

stories.headline: State House committee reviews hazard mitigation after tsunami and wildfire threats
stories.summary: The House Committee on Public Safety reviewed mitigation planning and lessons from recent evacuations, including traffic, fuel breaks, public education and readiness centers.
stories.text: The State House Committee on Public Safety held an informational briefing last Thursday To review hazard mitigation planning and after action reports on recent tsunami and wildfire threats. Officials detailed FEMA's multi-hazard mitigation planning process and outlined lessons from recent evacuations. The mitigation planning also highlighted traffic challenges, wildfire fuel breaks, ʻAprox, the need for stronger public education and community readiness centers.

stories.summary: Car dealers report other carriers from Asia are still bringing cars to Hawaii, so there was no negative effect on EVs after Matson stopped shipping them over battery fire risk.

stories.headline: Olinda Road paving work brings lane closures; look at road's condition
stories.summary: A package on the state-owned portion of Olinda Road says residents report that the state and county fight over jurisdiction while the county repairs its section.
stories.text: If there's a place that time forgot, or at least the state and county have forgotten, ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi, kūpuna, kū So from here on out, I mean, it's not bad. I mean, the county at least is taking care of its roads on Olinda. But the residents there told us that because the state and county continue to fight over who's got jurisdiction, no one's fixing their road. Maybe they should go back to public work school or something. I don't know. But once you get down past Oski Rice, it's clear sailing all the way to Makawao.

stories.headline: Lahainaluna beats King Kekaulike; Kamehameha Maui shuts out Maui High
stories.summary: Lahainaluna won 48-21 over King Kekaulike for the first time since 2004, and Kamehameha Maui beat a shorthanded Maui High 42-0.
stories.text: In MIL action, Lahaina Luna High School dominated the opening game of the Maui Interscholastic League, racking up an impressive 480 rushing yards in a 48-21 victory over King Kauauliki. The season breaks a long drought as Division II Lahaina Luna hadn't beaten Division I King Kauauliki in 35 matchups since 2004. Meanwhile, Division II defending state champion Kamehameha Maui cruised to a 42-0 rout over the short-handed Maui High School, which was missing key players due to injuries.
